Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial MSA redlines — UK addendum and SCCs

Rafael — thanks for taking this on.

As we discussed on the call last week, AcroHealth needs a clear path for UK transfers post-Brexit. Our GC has flagged two items that must be agreed before procurement can approve the order form: (1) an explicit UK addendum to be appended to Redwood’s DPA (we can provide our suggested language), and (2) confirmation that Redwood will accept the new EU SCCs + a mapped UK addendum where applicable.

I've attached our current redline of the MSA (redlined_MSA_v3.docx) and highlighted the transfer sections. Key asks:
- Who is the controller/processor responsible party mapping for EU->UK transfers?
- Confirmation on subprocessors in the UK and a timeline for providing the subprocessor list and SOC 2 evidence.
- A fallback if an SCC/UK addendum route is insufficient (we may need a transfer-addendum/manual binding mechanism).

Can your legal team provide a consolidated redline and a short note on the acceptable transfer mechanisms? Procurement is targeting signoff in the first half of June, so timing is tight.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a short sync.

Regards,
Tom Peterson
Head of Procurement, AcroHealth

On Wed, May 31, 2028 at 10:23 Rafael Mendes wrote:
> Tom — thanks for the clear summary...

Quick notes from Legal after a first pass (summary; see attached ben_clauses_notes.txt):
- SCCs / UK addendum: Redwood is prepared to adopt the EU SCCs. For UK transfers we will accept a UK addendum, but it must be limited to clarifying the data export obligations and cannot expand liability beyond the existing MSA cap.
- Controller/Processor mapping: propose language in DPA Exhibit A that explicitly enumerates responsibilities for export controls, encryption-at-rest, and access requests. Avoid ambiguous "as required by law" clauses that could broaden obligations.
- Subprocessors: we will provide the current subprocessor list and will commit to 30 days' notice for new subprocessors. AcroHealth has asked for evidence (SOC 2 / encryption attestations); we can provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II report in a redacted form and an internal encryption whitepaper.
- Fallback: If SCCs + UK addendum are rejected by your legal team, propose a limited transfer-addendum that references model clauses and includes a mutual mitigation plan (e.g., geo-routing for EU workloads). This would ideally be scoped to the specific order form and not the global MSA.

Action items for the sync:
- Agree on specific UK addendum language (Ben to propose minimal edits).
- Confirm whether AcroHealth needs execution via DocuSign or signed PDF (Tom to confirm).
- Request: AcroHealth to share any non-negotiable language (e.g., additional audit rights, extended liability for transfers).

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
Attachments: ben_clauses_notes.txt (plain text notes)
From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@acrohealth.com>

Rafael / Ben — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from AcroHealth Legal: 

1) We reviewed Redwood’s suggested language and flagged two items: (a) the proposed limitation on liability for transfer-related breaches — we require carveouts for willful misconduct and gross negligence to remain excluded from the cap; (b) we need a short clause that confirms Redwood will maintain the subprocessor list on an accessible page and notify customers by email 30 days before onboarding a new UK-based subprocessor.

2) We prefer execution via DocuSign; our procurement team will send the envelope once we receive the final consolidated redline.

3) Attached is our UK addendum draft (AcroHealth_UK-addendum_v1.docx). We included suggested text that mirrors the new EU SCCs but with an additional paragraph on UK ICO guidance compliance.

Tom is out of office til Wed; I can act as counterparty for legal redlines. We can accept the SOC 2 Type II report in redacted form for initial procurement review and then request a full review during onboarding.

Please confirm whether Redwood can accept the liability carveout language in principle (we can give sample drafting). If not, we’ll need to escalate to commercial for a limited exception.

Regards,
Sara Lin
Senior Counsel, AcroHealth

3) Subprocessor evidence: Redwood will share a redacted SOC 2 Type II report and an up-to-date subprocessor list within 48 hours of Ben’s redline. We confirm 30 days' notice for new subprocessors (we will publish the list on our customer portal).
